headline: Mainz favourites at home, but their own crowd is the question
summary: Mainz have scored 14 goals in their last 5 league games, and that attack is why they are clear favourites for Saturday's visit of Werder Bremen. The doubt sits at home: their last game at the Mewa Arena ended 3-4 to Bayer Leverkusen. Werder arrive unbeaten and have fought back to draw 3 league games in a row, with Niclas Füllkrug joint-top of the scoring charts according to bundesliga.com, though left-back Moussa Ndiaye is out. Mainz are 56.9% to win against Werder's 20.7%, rated about three-quarters of a goal the better side, with over 3.0 goals at 51%.
read: Mainz are clear 56.9% favourites, built on 2.56 xG per game and a run of five straight Bundesliga away wins — but both of their last two home games ended in defeat, 3-4 to Leverkusen and 1-3 to Frankfurt. Werder arrive unbeaten in five, having come back from two goals down in three straight games, with Füllkrug scoring in five in a row, so the market expects goals: about three of them, with both teams to score at 60.9%.

facts.fact: Mainz are clear favourites at 56.9% to win — nearly three times Werder's 20.7%.
facts.meaning: The home side is expected to take the game to Werder and win it in normal time.

facts.fact: Niclas Füllkrug has scored in five consecutive Bundesliga games and is joint-top of the scoring charts.
facts.meaning: Werder's route back into this game runs through a striker who has scored in every one of their last five league matches.

facts.fact: Mainz have averaged 2.56 xG over their last five games, well above Werder's 1.84.
Mainz's last five league results read W-L-W-L-W, with both defeats at home: 3-4 to Bayer Leverkusen and 1-3 to Eintracht Frankfurt.
facts.meaning: Their away form has carried them to fifth; at home they have conceded seven goals in their last two games.

facts.fact: Werder have come back from a two-goal deficit in three consecutive Bundesliga games, most recently 2-2 at home to Paderborn.
facts.meaning: They are unbeaten in five league games and do not fold when they go behind — a live underdog even at 20.7%.

facts.fact: Werder left-back Moussa Ndiaye is out of this match and the next two fixtures with persistent groin problems.
facts.meaning: Werder travel with their regular left side of defence reshuffled.

facts.fact: The market expects about three goals in this game, with Over 3.0 at 51%.
facts.meaning: More likely than not, this is a high-scoring afternoon at the Mewa Arena.

facts.fact: The market has both teams to score at 60.9%.
facts.meaning: Werder are expected to score even if they end up losing.

sources.fact: Mainz beat Schalke 04 1-0 last week and have now won five Bundesliga away games in a row, with the FAZ describing the Schalke display as one of Urs Fischer's side's best performances of the season.
German media point out a discrepancy between Mainz's away form and their home form, asking whether the team can finally deliver in front of their own crowd against Werder.
WELT reports that Mainz want to stay in touch with the top of the table with a result against Werder Bremen.
Robin Zentner and Silas have returned to full team training at Mainz, though a comeback in this match is reported to come too soon.
Silas has completed his first full training session since a serious leg injury as he steps up his Mainz comeback.
Mainz striker Phillip Tietz has five Bundesliga goals this season and is set for a direct duel with Werder's Niclas Füllkrug, according to the Bundesliga.
Left-back Moussa Ndiaye will miss Werder's Bundesliga match against Mainz and the following game against Hoffenheim, plus the DFB-Pokal tie with Borussia Dortmund, due to persistent groin problems.
Werder had to do without ten players in training ahead of the Mainz trip, though Justin Njinmah has returned, according to the Kreiszeitung.
